newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - NYMEX crude set for choppy range-trading.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - NYMEX crude set for choppy range-trading.

text.p: NYMEX crude futures looked set for a session of choppy range-trading on Friday with oil stock data fundamentals signalling a push higher but chartists warning that early gains could be reversed later on.

February crude closed 18 cents lower at $24.92 a barrel on Thursday but was trading 31 cents higher at 1355 GMT on ACCESS. January heating oil closed 1.34 cents lower at 70.06 but was up 1.09 cents on ACCESS.
Charles Gray at Prudential Bache said there was a good chance that any gap higher by crude at the open would be reversed later on.
"It could open at ACCESS levels around $25.20 and gap higher," he said referring to the pit-trade only chart. "But there's a good chance such a move would be reversed. The market's very twitchy."
"It's not uncommon to see reversals on the session after APIs," he added.
Gray saw crude hugging a $24.60/80 to $25.20 range during the session.
Al Graham at Elliott Wave International was similarly cautious about any upside breaks, although he said the bullish activity during ACCESS had softened his bearish stance.

"The penetration of $25.17 signals caution with respect to immediate bearish expectations, suggesting a pop above $25.33 before weakness resumes," he said in his daily Global Energy Outlook. "We need a deline below $25.05 to get things started on the downside."

On the heating oil front, Gray pinpointed support on the continuation chart around 69 cents and resistance at Thursday's high of 71.40 cents and then at the parametres of the downside gap between December 20 and 23 spanning 72.25 to 72.50.
Chartists at GNI noted that recent activity on heat's continuation chart had brought the complex dangerously close to breaching an upward trendline stretching back to June.

"It has been violated only twice, and on the last of these occasions closed above the line. The market is threatening it once more and this could be a significant technical signal," they wrote in their daily energy bulletin.
